cues: A runner eats the peeled fruit during a long training break, choosing an easy source of quick energy.
At camp, cooks slit the skin, tuck chocolate inside, wrap it in foil, and warm it over coals.
Some cooks flambé slices with rum, then spoon the caramelized fruit over vanilla ice cream for dessert.
Caregivers mash soft fruit through a fine sieve when preparing an early solid-food puree for babies.
In old slapstick routines, a performer drops a discarded peel before another character slips dramatically.
A roadside bakery folds sweet mashed fruit into pastry, sealing each turnover before baking it golden.
